title: Zero Dark Thirty
events_chronological: Over a black screen, emergency calls from inside the burning towers are heard on the morning of 11 September 2001.
Soon afterwards a source hands the CIA the real name of a bin Laden courier, Ibrahim Sayeed, and the report is filed away and forgotten.
In 2003 the CIA officer Maya arrives at a black site in Pakistan and watches her colleague Dan waterboard the detainee Ammar.
Broken by sleep deprivation and humiliation, Ammar gives up the existence of a courier called Abu Ahmed.
Maya works the detainee network for years, chasing the name through interrogations in Poland, Gdansk and Kuwait.
The 2005 London bombings and the 2008 Marriott bombing in Islamabad go off around her.
Maya's colleague Jessica cultivates a Jordanian informant who kills her and six others with a suicide vest at Camp Chapman in 2009.
Maya survives an assassination attempt by gunmen outside her Islamabad compound.
A detainee's account is matched against the buried 2001 report, and Abu Ahmed is identified as Ibrahim Sayeed.
Maya has the courier's mother's phone tapped, and he is finally located in Peshawar.
Surveillance follows the courier's white SUV to a fortified compound in Abbottabad with no telephone line and no internet.
Maya insists the compound is bin Laden's, and CIA director Panetta demands to know how certain she is.
The station chief and the analysts argue the probability down to sixty per cent, and Maya says one hundred.
The White House authorises a helicopter raid rather than an air strike, and two stealth Black Hawks are prepared.
SEAL Team Six flies into Abbottabad, and one helicopter's tail clips the compound wall as it lands.
The team clears the house floor by floor, killing the courier, his brother and Khalid bin Laden.
On the top floor they shoot bin Laden dead and carry the body out as the crippled helicopter is destroyed.
Maya identifies the body in a hangar at Jalalabad.
Maya boards a transport plane alone, is asked where she wants to go, and has no answer.
syuzhet_notes: The film runs forward through a decade, marked out with place and date captions, and its nonlinearity sits at the edges rather than the middle: told-order bullet 1 is a black screen of audio from two years before the story begins, and told-order bullet 9 reaches back to a report filed in 2001 that had been sitting unread in the CIA's own archive the whole time.
fabula_notes: The buried 2001 report is described rather than dramatised, and its position at the head of the chronology is established only by the late discovery of it. Long stretches of Maya's decade are compressed into captions, and bin Laden's own movements are never shown at all.
